thread:
acme-ops: Hey team — started getting a bunch of 500/parse errors when using structured JSON mode for generation. Happens intermittently, but today it's continuous. Response says 'Invalid JSON' and the body starts with '<!DOCTYPE html>'.

emily_support: Thanks, can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and the full response headers? Also which params are you sending (response_format, strict/json_mode)?

acme-ops: Repro below. We call with response_format=structured and json_strict=true. Accept: application/json. Response snippet and headers: 

```
$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"...","response_format":"structured","json_strict":true}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required\nContent-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8\nContent-Length: 1423\n\n<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html>\n<head><title>Billing required</title></head>\n<body>...invoice page...</body>\n</html>
```

The client-side parser throws 'invalid JSON: unexpected '<' at pos 0'. We only see this when json_strict is true — otherwise the SDK returns HTML as text. Guessing billing page is being returned for some requests.

jason_sre: OK that explains it — server returned an HTML payment page (402) not JSON. Two things to confirm: 1) Is the account hitting a billing block (402) or an auth 401? 2) Our strict enforcement in the SDK treats any non-application/json as parse error. Does the API ever return content-type 'application/json; charset=utf-8' instead of exact 'application/json'? That can also trigger strict checks if they're doing exact string compare.

maria_engineering: Quick notes from runtime team: our enforcement currently checks Content-Type startswith 'application/json' in hosted API, but some legacy edge path does exact equality and will reject 'application/json; charset=utf-8'. Also, we have a fallback gateway that rewrites some errors into HTML (billing page) when a downstream billing service responds.

emily_support: For now, workaround for the customer: turn off json_strict or add a try/catch around the structured parse and surface the raw body plus status code to the app. But we need actionable steps to avoid customers getting HTML in strict mode.

acme-ops: Workaround ok but we need stricter guarantees for production. Can you escalate? This is breaking our feature in prod and causing SLO breaches.

infra-bot: Escalation created: INC-2028-345. Assigned to eng-runtime + billing. Trace-id requested: please attach X-Request-Id from failing calls.

jason_sre: Next engineering steps I'm proposing:
- Confirm account billing state (billing team) and whether 402s are expected.
- Patch the legacy edge path to accept content-type with params (i.e. startswith check), and ensure SDK docs state that 'application/json; charset=utf-8' is acceptable.
- Add a 402->JSON fallback: if the upstream billing service returns JSON error, pass it through with JSON content-type; if it's HTML, return a small machine-readable JSON error (code/message) instead of raw HTML when response_format=structured or json_strict=true.

maria_engineering: I'll own the edge patch. ETA for a staged rollout: 1 business day for a hotfix to accept content-type params; 3 days to implement the 402->machine-json fallback and tests.

emily_support: Thanks. @acme-ops please send a few failing X-Request-Id values and exact timestamps (ms) so we can correlate logs. Also let us know if you want us to temporarily disable json_strict on your account until the fix lands. :+1:

acme-ops: Will send IDs now. Disabling strict temporarily would be helpful — please do that and update here. Appreciate the quick help. :relieved:

infra-bot: Customer setting updated: json_strict=false for account acme.corp (temporary flag). Logged by emily_support.
